subject: Accountancy
central_question: How can raw financial statements be reorganised and interpreted to reveal changes, relationships, strengths and weaknesses in a company’s performance and position?
in_scope_units: Meaning of financial statement analysis and interpretation.
Significance of analysis for management, investors, lenders, employees, government and other users.
Objectives of analysis: profitability, operational efficiency, solvency, liquidity and comparative performance.
Tools of analysis: comparative statements, common-size statements, trend analysis, ratio analysis and cash flow analysis.
Comparative Statement of Profit and Loss with absolute and percentage changes.
Comparative Balance Sheet and horizontal analysis of financial position.
Common-size Statement of Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet using a common base.
Horizontal, vertical, intra-firm and inter-firm analysis.
Limitations of financial analysis arising from source data, price changes, accounting methods, window dressing and non-monetary omissions.
banned_topics: Detailed ratio formulas and interpretation, which belong to Accounting Ratios.
Full preparation of the Cash Flow Statement, which belongs to Cash Flow Statement.
Original preparation and Schedule III presentation of company statements, which belong to Financial Statements of a Company.

known_pitfalls.claim: Analysis means merely calculating changes or percentages.
known_pitfalls.correction: Calculation organises information; interpretation explains the causes, significance and implications for decisions.

known_pitfalls.claim: A rise in every asset automatically proves improved performance.
known_pitfalls.correction: Asset changes must be related to financing, revenue, profit, liquidity and utilisation before a conclusion is drawn.

known_pitfalls.claim: Common-size statements show absolute rupee growth between years.
known_pitfalls.correction: They express each item as a percentage of a common base and are principally a vertical-analysis tool.

known_pitfalls.claim: Financial analysis removes the limitations of the original financial statements.
known_pitfalls.correction: Analysis inherits limitations relating to historical cost, policies, estimates, price changes and window dressing.

recommended_example_progression: Use Test Your Understanding–I to distinguish analysis from interpretation and identify user purposes.
Use NCERT Illustration 1 to prepare and interpret a Comparative Statement of Profit and Loss.
Use NCERT Illustrations 2–3 and the numerical exercises to prepare a Comparative Balance Sheet.
Use the common-size illustrations to express revenue items and Balance Sheet items as percentages of common bases.
Use Long Answer Questions 2–5 to compare tools and discuss their interpretation.
Use Section 4.7 and the end questions to evaluate limitations before drawing conclusions.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Questions for Practice containing Short Answer Questions 1–6, Long Answer Questions 1–5 and Numerical Questions on comparative and common-size statements.
